name: Hazael king of Syria
charge: Smothering his master to take the throne, and doing to Israel the evil Elisha wept over
summary: Elisha looked at Hazael and wept, and told him why: he knew the evil he would do to the children of Israel. Hazael said, Is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing? He went home, lied to his master about the prophet's word, and smothered him with a wet cloth the next morning.
offense: Ben-hadad sent Hazael to ask Elisha whether he would recover. Elisha spoke of recovery yet disclosed that the Lord had shown him the king would surely die. He then wept over the violence Hazael would bring upon Israel (2 Kings 8:7-12). Knowledge of an approaching reign did not turn its cruelties into good deeds. Hazael returned with the assurance of recovery but withheld the disclosure of death. The next day he spread a water-soaked cloth over the king's face, killed him, and reigned in his place (2 Kings 8:14-15). The messenger's access to a sick master became the means of taking his throne.
judgment: Hazael afterward struck Israel and reduced its territory (2 Kings 10:32-33). The Lord used Syrian power in chastening Israel, but that use did not place Syria beyond judgment for its violence. Elisha's tears had already distinguished the coming suffering from something to celebrate. Amos charged Damascus with threshing Gilead with iron instruments and pronounced fire upon the house of Hazael and the palaces of Ben-hadad, with Syria carried to Kir (Amos 1:3-5). The house that made others suffer was itself named for overthrow. Being an instrument in another people's punishment did not give its ruler ownership of their lives or immunity from the Lord's reckoning.

verses.text: And Elisha came to Damascus; and Ben–hadad the king of Syria was sick; and it was told him, saying, The man of God is come hither.
And the king said unto Hazael, Take a present in thine hand, and go, meet the man of God, and enquire of the Lord by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?

So Hazael went to meet him, and took a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Ben–hadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
And Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou mayest certainly recover: howbeit the Lord hath shewed me that he shall surely die.
And he settled his countenance stedfastly, until he was ashamed: and the man of God wept.

And Hazael said, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child.
And Hazael said, But what, is thy servant a dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha answered, The Lord hath shewed me that thou shalt be king over Syria.
So he departed from Elisha, and came to his master; who said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he answered, He told me that thou shouldest surely recover.
And it came to pass on the morrow, that he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.
In those days the Lord began to cut Israel short: and Hazael smote them in all the coasts of Israel;
From Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the river Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.
Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron:
But I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, which shall devour the palaces of Ben–hadad.

I will break also the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the plain of Aven, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the house of Eden: and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir, saith the Lord.
O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation.

I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.
Howbeit he meaneth not so, neither doth his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy and cut off nations not a few.

entries.commentary: Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines. When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life. The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days. Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child. Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife. He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon. This revolt fulfills the word spoken to Esau, that when he gained the dominion he would break the yoke from off his neck, a pattern reaching to Edom's later rise. Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. -

Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son. He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah. Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.

Jehu writes to the rulers of Jezreel who kept Ahab's seventy sons, challenging them to set up a son and fight, but they are exceedingly afraid because two kings could not stand before him. They submit as his servants, and Jehu's second letter commands them to take the heads of Ahab's seventy sons and bring them to Jezreel by the next day. The heads are laid in two heaps at the gate, and Jehu slays all that remained of the house of Ahab, his great men, kinsfolk, and priests, until none remained, according to the word spoken by Elijah.

Jehu meets the brethren of Ahaziah going to salute the king's children and has all forty-two of them slain at the pit of the shearing house, guilty by association with the house of Ahab. He takes up Jehonadab the son of Rechab, whose heart is right with his, into the chariot to see his zeal for the Most High. At Samaria Jehu slays all that remained unto Ahab, destroying him according to the saying of the Most High spoken to Elijah.

Jehu gathers all the worshippers of Baal by pretending he will serve Baal much more than Ahab did, doing it in subtilty to destroy them. He fills the house of Baal, brings out vestments for every worshipper, and makes sure no servant of the Most High is among them, only Baal worshippers, as with the clergy garments and idolatry seen in false worship today. After the sacrifice he sends in the guard to slay them all, breaks down the images and the house of Baal, and makes it a draught house, so Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel. -

Though Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel, he does not depart from the golden calves that Jeroboam set up in Bethel and in Dan; hold Dan in mind for later scriptures. The Most High commends Jehu for executing what is right against the house of Ahab and promises his children to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel. Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin. -

In those days the Most High begins to cut Israel short, and Hazael smites them in all the coasts from Jordan eastward through Gilead and Bashan. The rest of Jehu's acts are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel, and he reigns twenty-eight years in Samaria before Jehoahaz his son reigns in his place. Jehu's life is a warning that the walk is a marathon, not a sprint, and the difference is whether a man gets back up and repents or stays down and departs from the law. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

Woe is pronounced on those who decree unrighteous decrees and write grievous laws to turn aside the needy from judgment and take away the right from the poor. That is us: we are the needy, we are the poor. Back then this was the Assyrians doing it to us because of our disobedience. Today it is your friendly neighborhood white man writing unrighteous laws and prescribing them for us to keep. It is a twofold prophecy. The unrighteous decrees rob the widows and the fatherless. The question is put to the oppressor: what will you do in the day of visitation and desolation, to whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory. Without the Most High they bow down under the prisoners and fall under the slain, for His anger is not turned away and His hand is stretched out still.

The Most High calls the Assyrian the rod of His anger, the staff in their hand His indignation. He used nations to punish us. He sends the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation, the people of His wrath, to take the spoil and tread them down like the mire of the streets. The Most High calls us hypocrites because we love to say we love the Most High, but we do not want to do what the Bible says. The Assyrian did not mean it that way; it was in his heart to destroy and cut off nations. He boasted of the kingdoms he conquered and their idols, not realizing the Most High was using him to punish us and the rest of the nations. We had graven images throughout our land, breaking the Most High's laws.

When the Most High has finished His work on Zion and Jerusalem, He will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria and the glory of his high looks. The Assyrian said, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am prudent," boasting that he removed the treasures and inhabitants of the people on his own. The Most High asks whether the axe boasts against the one who hews with it, or the saw magnifies itself against the one who shakes it. The Assyrian was only the axe; the Most High used him to cut us down from rulership to captivity. Therefore the Most High sends leanness among the fat ones and kindles a burning fire that devours the thorns and briers in one day and consumes the glory of the forest, both soul and body, until the trees are so few a child may write them.

In that day the remnant of Israel and those who escaped of the house of Jacob shall no more stay upon him that smote them, but stay upon the Most High, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. This is a future prophecy. "Stay" means to rely upon. Just like back then, we still rely upon the ones who smote us, even today under the nation of Edom, trusting in oppression, relying on the very ones still smiting us in the streets. In that day the remnant, those keeping the Most High's commandments in their right mind, will escape and stop leaning on the oppressor. Though Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant shall return. The Most High will make a consumption decreed and overflowing with righteousness in the midst of all the land. -

The Most High tells His people who dwell in Zion not to be afraid of the Assyrian who smites with a rod and lifts up his staff after the manner of Egypt, for in a very little while the indignation will cease and His anger will turn to their destruction. The Most High will stir up a scourge for the Assyrian, and his yoke shall be taken off Israel's neck and destroyed because of the anointing. The chapter traces the invader's march through the towns until he shakes his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion. Then the Most High of hosts lops the bough with terror, the high ones are hewn down, and Lebanon falls by a mighty one.

An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.
